thread.title: Earth Awaits Enphase Energy's Microgrid - Enphase Energy Inc. (NASDAQ:ENPH)

author: TJ Roberts
title: Earth Awaits Enphase Energy's Microgrid - Enphase Energy Inc. (NASDAQ:ENPH)
text:
The world is awaiting IQ8 Ensemble, Enphase Energy’s ( ENPH ) revolutionary microgrid solution which is grid-independent and doesn't need batteries to operate; it is an intelligent solution that can dynamically match the electrical loads in your home with your solar system’s current output. Like all of Enphase’s products, IQ8 microgrid will come with unmatched reliability, safety, longevity, performance and simplicity ( easy to install/easy to manage ). Read on to understand what's in store for Enphase Energy.
The beauty of Enphase, and something they parallel with Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) is their “ cool ” products which are easy to install and manage. Enphase has really pushed the limits of residential solar by making their hardware easily installable by the DIY-er, thereby creating a much wider installer audience than the competition's. Furthermore, by holding the title for the fastest installable solar system , Enphase gives installers the highest possible productivity currently available. The fact that Enphase's simple IQ8 microgrid will require limited to no installer involvement will make the product more appealing to the masses, especially when compared to the competitions' more complex solutions.
As a local installer on a small scale, I already have 10 parties who are willing to visit my home just to see me shut off my service panel's master switch, and for Enphase’s microgrid to take over and provide grid-independent power. Like the Dot-com revolution which gave freedom of communication and information, Enphase’s microgrid is going to do the same in the power arena, and the freedom achieved will be from the centralized utilities; their days of monopolized power are numbered in the residential arena, for solar and storage are gaining momentum. Recent SunPower (NASDAQ: SPWR )-Enphase and SunPower-Sonnen announcements exemplify that.
My solar system ROI will be achieved in 2019 after 7 productive years without a single microinverter problem or downtime. I used to have a ~$400 monthly utility bill living here in hot, humid Florida ( had it not been for A/C, Florida would have never grown to be the 3rd most populous state in the U.S.! ). Like many solar system owners who have had their system for a lengthy period and have realized its value, “ retrofitting ” or upgrading to Enphase IQ8 microgrid will be highly desirable. It really just comes down to product availability because it's not a full-blown solar install, but an upgrade that will give existing systems more value than it initially had. Furthermore, many Enphase customers are awaiting the IQ8 Battery, the second major revision of the AC Battery product. Remember, Enphase had been working on a dual-charge ACB which would have been a 275/550W model back in the 2014-15 time frame; therefore, a 320/640W version or better could be in the works. Enphase's co-founder and CPO, Raghu Belur, said in the Q4 2017 earnings call that along with IQ8, Enphase will have a " new AC Battery configuration with a great cost structure ".
To hint at just how big Enphase’s microgrid market is going to be, consulting firm McKinsey estimated in June that microgrid ( off-grid ) solar systems could benefit as many as 150M households by 2020. If Enphase were to even reap 25% of that market, it would bring them to an easy multi-billion dollar market capitalization. According to CEO Jim Jenal of Run on Sun , a Tier-1 solar installation company in California, " Run on Sun and its clients are eagerly awaiting ” IQ8; with this microcosm, surely many more are waiting, too. The fact that Enphase continues to add more major distributors and partners ( SunPower, Solaria, Panasonic ( OTCPK:PCRFY ), LG ( OTC:LGEAF ), JinkoSolar ( JKS ) and Waaree Energies ) signifies the company's continuous growth.
Consider the markets where IQ8 is going to debut first in the developing countries. Remote regions with weak or no power grids in place will be ground zero for IQ8. The World Bank pointed to a $450B " remittance " for 2017, an increase of ~5% for " developing countries "; this is important, for it reflects all the foreign workers in the United States, Europe and Russia with roots in countries like Sub-Saharan Africa, Europe, Central Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean. A simple DIY IQ8 microgrid would be ideal for these market regions, and it will be a simple fit due to its affordability and low-entry price-tag when compared to competing microgrid solutions from Tesla ( TSLA ), SolarEdge ( SEDG ), and others, plus IQ7 going forward is a " universal " product for global markets, optimizing Enphase's single-product service strategy.
In the " remittance " market regions which represent Enphase's " Rest of World " or RoW market outside of the USA, Enphase is looking at a new chunk of that 4-10GW SAM it had mentioned last year. Taking the Philippines as a good " remittance " microcosm, their household energy & transportation takes 7.8% of the budget, with non-food spending at ~15%. Since " remittance " is largely used for living rather than disposable income, this percentage seems fair to say. Thus, out of that 2017 $450B figure, $45-70B is used for household energy & transportation where maybe 50% is used for electricity, so approximately $20-35B. Now, considering the 5-year ROI hurdle for the $100-175B solar system market with an average $1,000-1,500 system cost, that's ~100M systems. Enphase traditionally holds 25-30% in the markets they operate in, not including the latest SunPower marriage, so that is a reservoir of ~25M systems or 25 x 3 microinverters or a 75M-microinverter opportunity or $7.5B revenue potential in the " remittance " market; it will likely take an 8-year growth to get there.

Enphase has ~760k customers already; let’s guesstimate ~200k are 5th-gen S-series, IQ6 or IQ7 customers; surely they will want to upgrade, since their entire system can be a microgrid without having to replace any microinverters. For the ~500k legacy M-series customers though, they may have to replace microinverters if they want to partake in the microgrid. Both scenarios are simple “ retrofit ” operations since the only non-roof work is the Envoy upgrade, and the roof-work is just swapping out microinverters, cabling and possibly panels. For the ~760k Enphase base, there is no logical reason why clients would not want to go microgrid — no batteries, no gas, no propane, nothing needed except sunshine and your existing solar system. Let’s take half of the ~760k Enphase base with each spending ~$5k to upgrade; that’s a ~$2B market right there. I am a legacy M-series customer waiting on the virtual Enphase IQ8 Reservation List , and here in Hurricane Alley ( Florida, the Sunshine State ), IQ8 will be a godsend. I have asked 14 Enphase customers whether they will be upgrading to IQ8 after being explained the technology, and all but one said “ yes ”; they are patiently awaiting IQ8.
The IQ8 represents a ~26% parts-reduction to the current IQ7 product, and its microgrid capability ( Ensemble software ) will add value to the product that has never existed before; the IQ9, which is due at the end of 2019, will approach an even lower production cost; these reductions will allow Enphase's product to compete effectively in C/I, as well as residential solar, and will reduce OpEx considerably. The AC Battery , Envoy , Combiner Box , and Aggregator are all high-margin “ non-inverter revenue ” accessories for Enphase, and the CFO said at the Q1 2018 earnings conference that accessory revenue continues to increase “ as a percentage of revenue compared to prior quarter results ”; in a retrofit setting, this revenue will only increase in a non-linear fashion since many systems will not need to replace all their microinverters.
Make no mistake, IQ8 is going to be the Holy Grail of microinverters and microgrid solutions. It will take Enphase's current residential market with some C/I and propel the company into a whole new and much bigger market whose size has been estimated ( McKinsey ), but in all reality, is unfathomable. The Earth needs Enphase’s simple microgrid solution to provide power, independent of the utilities, or where none currently exists or is unreliable ( India, Africa, etc ). I believe Enphase Energy is undervalued because people do not understand the patented technology Enphase has been testing for over a year and is about to release. I would love to look into a crystal ball and see a year or two out for this company. Would we see major growth? Reports on Enphase India at 50 employees in less than a year shed a positive light on that answer; Enphase India still has a ways to go to get to the 700 employees that Kothandaraman built for TJ Rodgers decades ago for Cypress India ( CY ), but it's happening. IQ8 is going to be a game changer for Enphase Energy, the Earth, and maybe even Mars , so hold on shareholders!
